details:
Aureva – Personalized Astronaut Health Monitoring System

What exactly does it do?

Aureva is a personalized astronaut health monitoring system designed to help astronauts understand, track, and manage their health during long-duration space missions, particularly when immediate medical assistance is unavailable and communication with Earth is delayed.

Inspired by NASA's Human Research Program and its five major hazards of spaceflight, Aureva focuses on important health indicators, including heart rate, radiation exposure, sleep quality, mood, cardiovascular health, immune response, and bone density.

Unlike traditional health monitoring dashboards, Aureva focuses on personalized health baselines. Instead of comparing every astronaut against the same standard values, it helps identify unusual changes in each individual's health patterns.

The system provides interactive health dashboards, 7-day and 30-day trend analysis, personalized mission insights, daily health check-ins, and shareable health reports.

How does it work?

Aureva combines research-based health indicators, data analysis, and machine learning to identify potential abnormalities in astronaut health patterns.

We used NASA's space health research and data to develop our project dataset, incorporating simulated astronaut health measurements for prototype testing.

To analyze health patterns and explore anomaly detection, we experimented with seven machine learning algorithms:

  • Isolation Forest
  • Local Outlier Factor (LOF)
  • One-Class Support Vector Machine (One-Class SVM)
  • K-Means Clustering
  • Random Forest
  • K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN)
  • XGBoost

We evaluated these models to identify a suitable approach for detecting unusual health patterns and integrated the selected model's output into the Aureva frontend.

The system presents health information through easy-to-understand visualizations. Astronauts can monitor their current health indicators, review historical trends, and receive actionable insights when measurements deviate from their personalized baselines.

For example, if an astronaut's resting heart rate rises above their usual baseline, Aureva can highlight the change and suggest reviewing sleep and recovery patterns.

Astronauts can also complete a quick daily health check-in and generate health summaries that can be shared with medical professionals when communication becomes available.

What benefits does it have?

Aureva aims to improve astronaut health awareness, independence, and informed decision-making during space missions.

Its key benefits include:

  • Personalized monitoring: Tracks individual health baselines rather than relying only on general population averages.
  • Early risk awareness: Uses machine learning to help identify unusual changes in health patterns.
  • Actionable insights: Transforms complex health measurements into understandable information and suggested actions.
  • Long-term trend analysis: Helps astronauts recognize gradual health changes through 7-day and 30-day visualizations.
  • Greater astronaut independence: Supports self-monitoring when immediate access to medical professionals is limited.
  • Improved health communication: Allows astronauts to generate organized health reports for medical review.

What do we hope to achieve?

Our mission is to empower astronauts to recognize potential health risks early, understand their body's signals, and make informed health decisions during missions to the Moon, Mars, and beyond.

Currently, Aureva is a research-based prototype using simulated astronaut health data. Our long-term goal is to develop it into a more comprehensive health monitoring and decision-support system.

Future improvements include integrating real-time wearable sensors, introducing telemedicine capabilities, expanding the monitoring of spaceflight-related health risks, improving machine learning analysis, and generating more advanced health reports.

We also hope to adapt Aureva to different space environments, including spacecraft, lunar bases, and Mars missions.

What tools, technologies, and hardware did we use?

Programming and frontend technologies:

  • JavaScript
  • HTML
  • CSS

Machine Learning:

  • Isolation Forest
  • Local Outlier Factor
  • One-Class SVM
  • K-Means
  • Random Forest
  • KNN
  • XGBoost

Research and data sources:

  • NASA Human Research Program and space health research data
  • NASA's five hazards of human spaceflight
  • Canadian Space Agency research on astronaut radiation monitoring
  • Simulated astronaut health data for prototype development and testing

Software and development tools:

  • Vercel for web application deployment
  • ChatGPT for presentation script preparation and selected visual content generation
  • Claude AI for backend troubleshooting and development assistance

Hardware:

  • Intel Core i5 12th Generation processor-based computer for development, model experimentation, and testing

The current prototype operates using simulated data and does not yet require specialized medical hardware or connected wearable sensors.

Conclusion

Aureva represents our vision of making astronaut health monitoring more personalized, understandable, and accessible.

By combining NASA-inspired space health research, machine learning, personalized health baselines, and a user-friendly interface, we aim to create a foundation for future astronaut health monitoring systems.

Our goal is simple: help astronauts understand what their bodies are telling them, even when they are millions of miles away from Earth.
